text.p: London gold fixed at $345.00 per ounce on Friday morning, the lowest since September 14, 1993, as rumours swirled of more central bank sales.
Bullion, which has plunged from about $370 at the start of the year, fixed at $349.25 on Thursday afternoon.
"It is not confirmed but everyone is saying that a central bank has been selling," a European-based bullion dealer said.

Gold has also been shunned by investors who prefer to pour money into booming U.S. stock markets, which have recovered over the past few days and put the Dow Industrial average back within reach of its all-time high.

Bullion's lustre has dimmed since last year when a blistering rally took the spot price to about $416. News earlier this month that the Dutch central bank sold 300 tonnes of gold further dented confidence.
Analysts say the market may find some buying around $341, with important support at $330, the low of 1993.
